newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cult guru admits blame for subway gas attack.
newsitem.headline: Japan cult guru admits blame for subway gas attack.

text.p: The Japanese cult guru on trial for masterminding last year's Tokyo subway gas attack said for the first time on Friday that he bore all responsibility for the tragedy.

"Regarding this case, I would like to shoulder all responsibility," Shoko Asahara suddenly told the judge at the Tokyo District Court during cross examination of one of his top disciples. "Please stop questioning him."
It was the first time that Asahara, head of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect), had publicly admitted to the attack, which killed 11 and made some 6,000 ill.

Asahara, who was arrested in May 1995, has been indicted on 17 charges ranging from murder and attempted murder to illegal production of drugs and weapons. He faces the death penalty by hanging if convicted.
"I was instructed by God in my detention cell this morning," said the 41-year-old Asahara, whose real name is Chizuo Matsumoto.
Asahara made his surprise admission during questioning by his defence lawyers of Yoshihiro Inoue, the guru's top lieutenant in the March 20, 1995 subway attack.
The prosecution had called Inoue as one of its witnesses in Asahara's six-month-long trial for murder in the March 1995 gas attack.
Since his arrest, Inoue has spoken out against Asahara, saying the guru directly ordered the attack.
The court went into early recess after Asahara's statement.

About 30 of Asahara's top lieutenants have also been indicted for the subway gassing, the murder of a follower who tried to quit the group, use of illegal drugs and attempts to mass-produce Russian-designed automatic weapons.
The 10,000-member Aum Shinri Kyo has been accused of using the nerve gas sarin in the subway and other attacks.
The first gas attack was in July 1994 in the mountain resort city of Matsumoto where seven people died and 600 were made ill.
